hypothesis.statement: fn_800C03E0's whole surviving residual is now a callee-saved PERMUTATION plus one word, and the permutation is anchored by the three initialised pointer locals, whose defining instructions were read out of both streams by `savedregs.py` rather than inferred. TWO WEBS ALREADY AGREE: tblA, defined in BOTH streams at `@0x18 addi r27,r3,0  @lbl_802C45C...`, and shift, defined in BOTH at `@0x28 li r23,10`. THE THREE THAT DO NOT, quoted as first definitions: fmts is target `@0x20 addi r26,r4,0  @lbl_8011645...` against ours `@0x20 addi r28,r4,0  @lbl_8011645...`; tblB is target `@0x24 addi r28,r3,0  @lbl_80127DE...` against ours `@0x24 addi r29,r3,0  @lbl_80127DE...`; div is target `@0x34 mr r30,r0` against ours `@0x34 mr r26,r0`. The two line/qline webs follow: target `@0x50 li r29,20` and `@0x58 li r31,20` against ours `@0x50 li r31,20` and `@0x58 li r30,20`. Every one of those pairs sits at the SAME offset in both streams, so the emission slot is already right and only the colour is wrong. The next lane should move ONE web at a time within the initialised-local class -- swap the declaration positions of `fmts` and `tblB`, which are adjacent, both initialised pointers, and the only two whose defining instruction is an ADDR16_LO materialisation of a different symbol -- and re-read savedregs after each, rather than reordering the whole list. The declaration-order class is expected to reach codegen for these two (unlike `div`, whose initialiser probe folded away) precisely because their defining instructions differ in the relocated symbol, not just the register field.
